title: Audit fixes: approvals, recovery, verification and less repeated work

snapshot.branch: main at 0b4e4b4. Local commits are not pushed.
snapshot.basis: A read-only audit by six subagents plus spot checks in the main session, on 2026-11-03 at 0b4e4b4 (package 2.8.0-rc.1, rules 1.8.0). Nothing is built yet.

understanding: You want the defects from the audit fixed so that workflow-axa takes fewer unauthorized actions, recovers more clearly and repeats less work. The fixes change package files only and keep the four phases, both gates and the report design.

requirements.text: After /workflow, application code edits and git writes are allowed only when the current task's Approval line approves the current revision. The user's words that the line quotes must appear in a real user message. Loading clarify or specify allows only task records and the report.
Negated or quoted "lightweight" wording grants nothing. A lightweight edit needs a recorded line that names its files.
Another task's approval does not authorize the current task. A valid approval survives resumption. A changed scope does not inherit it.
Reading a phase SKILL.md whole counts as loading that phase, as the router documents.

The gate also runs for the PowerShell tool and MCP write tools. It catches common shell writes: redirection, tee, cp, mv, Set-Content, git apply, git checkout and git reset. The docs say plainly that command-text filtering is advice, not a security boundary.
An interrupted record write leaves the old file intact. A concurrent change is refused, never silently lost.

"Stop" ends implementation: no review loop and no return to execute. Paused, blocked, cancelled and partial each have one clear route. The handoff names what changed, what was verified, what remains and the next safe action.
A failure counts as existing only when the same test fails the same way. Five existing failures that become four existing plus one new are reported as one new failure.
A baseline is reused only while its command, commit, diff and environment still match. The required checks run again after the last repair.

A small change uses one builder and one independent review. A small change is one ticket with named files and no interface, data, dependency or security change. It leaves that route when it turns risky. An unchanged diff gets no second review.

Words that carry uncertainty, permission or a proposal keep their meaning. The wording check runs before the report is written, never blocks a valid report and covers every report kind. An approved or presented report is never overwritten. A report counts as presented once the task records name it.
The test suite passes in a path with spaces and under POSIX.
One current verification summary exists. It is tied to a commit and an environment and is generated where practical. The other documents point to it.
A release package is built from an explicit include list, without Git internals, caches, secrets or evaluation output.

boundaries: Only workflow-axa package files change: hooks, scripts, skills, docs and tests.
No application repository changes, no global settings or permission changes and no automatic commits.
The four phases, grilling, grounded planning, both gates, task reuse, history, shared rules and artifact protections stay.
Pinned specialist methods, the D14 UI rule and the approved report design stay.
No package code changes before you agree to the behavior and approve the plan.

evidence.claim: After /workflow, loading workflow-clarify alone allows an Edit of application code and git push. session_state turns any phase name in the transcript into one yes or no, and clarify counts the same as execute.
evidence.limits: Reproduced with probe scripts at 0b4e4b4. The probes and logs are in the session scratchpad, outside the repository. Also rechecked by hand.

evidence.claim: Chat text "This is NOT a lightweight edit" grants the lightweight exemption, because LIGHTWEIGHT matches the bare phrase in any assistant text.
evidence.limits: Reproduced with probe scripts at 0b4e4b4. The probes and logs are in the session scratchpad, outside the repository. Also rechecked by hand.

evidence.claim: A phase loaded for task A satisfies the check for a new task B later in the same session.
evidence.limits: Reproduced with probe scripts at 0b4e4b4. The probes and logs are in the session scratchpad, outside the repository.

evidence.claim: The gate misses many shell writes, for example redirection, tee, cp, mv, Set-Content, git apply, git checkout -- file and git reset --hard. A records path anywhere in a command exempts the whole command, and the cd target is judged instead of the written file.
evidence.limits: Reproduced with probe scripts at 0b4e4b4. The probes and logs are in the session scratchpad, outside the repository.

evidence.claim: A whole read of a phase SKILL.md does not count as loading the phase, so edits stay blocked. The router documents that read as its fallback.
evidence.limits: Reproduced with probe scripts at 0b4e4b4. The probes and logs are in the session scratchpad, outside the repository.

evidence.claim: The PowerShell tool and MCP write tools are outside the hooks.json matcher, so the gate never runs for them.
evidence.limits: Read from hooks.json. The matcher is Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|Bash.

evidence.claim: It is unknown which transcript a subagent's hook call receives. If it is the subagent's own transcript, it has no /workflow line and is not gated.
evidence.limits: Unknown. Not reproduced.

evidence.claim: The agent can write the PLAN.md Approval line itself, because task records are writable before approval. The real user answer is a user message in the transcript, which the hook can read.
evidence.limits: A limit, not a reproduced defect.

evidence.claim: workflow-execute and phase_reads.py require a fresh worker for every ticket, a fresh reviewer, and a re-review of every repair, record-only repairs included. workflow-deliver requires a fresh reconciler.
evidence.limits: Read from the instructions.

evidence.claim: Measured runs: one-ticket rename r22-short used 4 agents, $9.25 and 84 turns. r22-long used 11 agents, $16.35 and 133 turns. Its T2 review and its whole-feature review started 9 seconds apart on the same unchanged diff.
evidence.limits: Costs are running totals from the headless summaries of this session.

evidence.claim: The baseline records failure counts only. Five existing failures that become four existing plus one new pass as unchanged. The rules library already says to compare actual tests, not totals.
evidence.limits: Read from the instructions.

evidence.claim: A baseline records no command, commit, diff state or environment, so a resumed session can reuse a stale one.
evidence.limits: Read from the instructions.

evidence.claim: No rule says that the required checks run again after the last repair, and task_report.py cannot detect a stale check itself.
evidence.limits: Read from the instructions and the helper.

evidence.claim: In a checkout path with spaces, 11 tests fail because activate_rules.py refuses such paths. Under WSL, 2 tests fail because a test reads the live D:/workflow-axa checkout.
evidence.limits: The 11 Windows skips are real host limits. The POSIX run executed them and they passed.

evidence.claim: hooks.json runs python. On a host with only python3, no hook starts, so the gate enforces nothing.
evidence.limits: A risk. Not reproduced on such a host.

evidence.claim: simple-english bans should, would, may, might and could, and task_report.py flags them. WRITING.md requires must, may and must not to be kept. Following the advice can turn an unproven cause into a false certainty.
evidence.limits: Read from the skills and the helper.

evidence.claim: render_report.py writes the HTML first and runs the wording check after. --open opens the file even with problems. Review reports without a task_report block get no wording check.
evidence.limits: Read from the renderer.

evidence.claim: --replace-unpresented checks only that the renderer made the file, so it would overwrite an approved report. Three documents still say that every re-render needs a new file.
evidence.limits: Read from the renderer and the docs.

evidence.claim: Measured: the mulcol task made plan-r1, -v2 and -v3 within two minutes, and all three were opened.
evidence.limits: This happened before --replace-unpresented existed.

evidence.claim: record.py writes in place. A kill during the write leaves an empty or cut-off record. Two writers at once lose one write. tick T1 can tick T1.2 and turns a cancelled line into a ticked one.
evidence.limits: Reproduced with probe scripts at 0b4e4b4. The probes and logs are in the session scratchpad, outside the repository.

evidence.claim: A user's "stop" routes to deliver. Deliver requires the whole-feature review or hands back to execute, and execute repeats while a ticket is ready. No stopped, paused or cancelled state exists.
evidence.limits: Read from the instructions.

evidence.claim: The docs contradict each other on the skill count (20 or 21), the rules version (1.6.0 or 1.8.0), the test count and the browser and host checks. VALIDATION names no source commit.
evidence.limits: Read from README, CHANGELOG, VALIDATION, UPGRADE and VENDORED-SKILLS.

evidence.claim: No release or ZIP tool exists, although VALIDATION describes one. No inclusion policy and no root LICENSE exist. No secret-like files were found.
evidence.limits: Read from the repository files.

sections.title: Request
sections.text:
Fix the defects that the owner's audit found in workflow-axa 2.8.0-rc.1. The goal is fewer unauthorized actions, clearer recovery and less repeated work. The goal is not more instructions or a larger test count.

This is a separate task. It fixes defects in the package that the task 2026-11-02-modular-engineering-workflow built.
sections.locator: PLAN.md ## Goal and acceptance; ## Current checkpoint, Task identity

sections.title: What will change
sections.text:
Edits and git writes get permission only from the current task's approval, with the user's real words. The gate sees more tools and more shell writes.

Record writes become safe against interruption and a second writer. A stop ends implementation, and each unfinished state has one route. Baselines compare test IDs and stop being reused when their inputs change.

Report wording advice keeps the meaning and runs before the file is written. A small change uses fewer agents. The tests pass on other machines. One generated summary replaces the contradicting counts, and a release package comes from an include list.

Not included: application repositories, global settings, permission changes and automatic commits.

Your answers D1 to D5 are part of it. Approval needs the Approval line plus your real words. Small changes use the small route. The project gets an MIT license and a release tool now. T9 uses at most 8 live Claude runs plus useful Codex runs.
sections.locator: PLAN.md ## Agreement; ## Goal and acceptance A1-A14; ## Approach and scope

sections.title: How it will be built
sections.text:
Nine tickets, ordered by impact. First come T1 approvals, T2 records and T3 stop and recovery. Then come T4 baselines, T5 reports and wording, T6 proportional agents, T7 portability, T8 docs and release and T9 live acceptance.

The main session builds each ticket. Only package files change: hooks, scripts, skills, docs and tests.

sections.title: Order of work
sections.text:
T1, T2, T5 and T7 depend on no other ticket. T3 follows T2, because it uses the records that T2 writes. T4 and T6 follow T3.

T8 follows T1 to T7, because it documents their final state. T9 follows T1 to T6 and stays within the D5 limit.

sections.title: Decisions
sections.text:
You answered Q1 to Q5 on 2026-11-03.

D1 (Q1): "Line + your real words". Code edits and git writes need the current task's Approval line, and the user's words that it quotes must appear in a real user message.

D2 (Q2): "1 builder + 1 review". The small route in T6 applies, with the escalation rule.

D3 (Q3): "MIT." T8 adds an MIT LICENSE at the root.

D4 (Q4): "Build the release tool now." T8 adds tools/build_release.py.

D5 (Q5): "Allow up to 8 Claude runs plus Codex runs where useful, but avoid unnecessary paid runs." T9 stays within that limit.

sections.title: Risks and assumptions
sections.text:
The hook blocks the explicit edit tools that it sees. It cannot see every shell write or edits outside Claude Code. It cannot prove that a record is true beyond matching the user's words in the transcript. Codex gets no hooks. The docs will say so.

It is unknown which transcript a subagent's hook call receives (E7). If it is the subagent's own, the subagent is not gated. T1 finds out and then gates subagents or documents the gap.

A host with only python3 starts no hook (E15). Live runs cost about $1 to $17 each, so D5 limits them to 8 Claude runs plus useful Codex runs.
sections.locator: PLAN.md ## Approach and scope, Enforcement honesty; FINDINGS E7, E8, E15; TODO.md T1

sections.title: How it will be checked
sections.text:
Each confirmed defect gets a regression test that fails before the fix. The full package suite runs once per ticket and once at the end.

T1, T2 and T3 each get one fresh reviewer. The other tickets get one combined review at the end. Live runs: at most 8 Claude runs plus Codex runs where useful (D5), and no run is repeated without a reason.

tickets.specification:
Permission comes from the current task's PLAN.md Approval line for the current revision, in the worktree of the edited file. The user's words that the line quotes must appear in a real user message. Clarify and specify allow records and the report only. A whole read of a phase SKILL.md counts as loading it. A lightweight edit needs a recorded line that names files.

The hooks.json matcher adds the PowerShell tool and MCP write tools. More shell write patterns are caught, and paths are resolved. Explicit edit tools fail closed when the transcript cannot be read. A short section says what is enforced.

T1 also settles E7. A hook log in a fixture run shows which transcript a subagent's hook call receives. Then T1 gates subagents or documents the gap.
tickets.expected: Each E1-E7 bypass is blocked, and each legitimate route still works. One fresh reviewer reviews the ticket.

tickets.specification: record.py writes to a temp file in the same folder, copies the file mode and replaces the record. It refuses the write when the file changed since it was read, with a hash check under a lock file. new creates the file exclusively. tick matches the exact ID and never ticks a cancelled line. A BOM and mixed line endings are kept.
tickets.expected: An interrupted or concurrent write never empties a record or loses a change. One fresh reviewer reviews the ticket.

tickets.specification: Add the stopped, paused and cancelled states. Stop goes to the partial record in deliver without a review loop. Blocked is not done. A failed review stops after two tries with a recorded reason. The lightweight path skips the whole-feature check. The handoff lists changed files, verified work, remaining work and the next safe action.
tickets.expected: Each state has one route, and a stop never returns to building. One fresh reviewer reviews the ticket.

tickets.specification: The baseline records failing test IDs with their first error line, plus the command, the commit, a diff hash and the environment. A new compare_failures.py compares two runs. The baseline is reused only while all inputs match. The required checks run again after the last repair.
tickets.expected: A new failure is reported even when the count stays the same. A changed input invalidates the baseline.

tickets.specification: Uncertainty, permission and proposal words become advice that keeps the meaning. Quoted and code text is exempt. The check runs before the file is written, for every report kind. --open does not run while problems remain. --replace-unpresented refuses a file that the task records name, shown or approved, and a file with approved state. The docs agree with the renderer.
tickets.expected: The five audit sentences keep their meaning. A shown or approved report cannot be replaced. Repeated wording fixes keep one file.

tickets.specification: Add the small route and its escalation rule. Parallel workers run only for independent tickets with separate files. A repair to records or wording needs no re-review. The last ticket's review counts as the whole-feature review when nothing changed after it. Reconciliation reuses the reviewer on the small route.
tickets.expected: A one-ticket change uses fewer agent calls than r22-short, and no unchanged diff is reviewed twice.

tickets.specification: Tests build paths from the checkout root. Activation tests use a temporary library without spaces, plus one test that expects the refusal. The doctor reports when python is missing.
tickets.expected: The suite passes in a path with spaces and under WSL.

tickets.specification: Add a generated Current verification section with the commit, the environment, the commands and the results. validate.py rejects skill or version counts in prose that differ from plugin.json. Add tools/build_release.py with an explicit include list. Add an MIT LICENSE at the root (D3).
tickets.expected: The docs give one set of counts, and the release package lists no excluded path.

tickets.specification: Run headless Claude sessions on fixtures for each bypass and each legitimate route, and Codex runs where they are useful. D5 allows at most 8 Claude runs and no unnecessary paid runs.
